content: If you are allergic to this medication, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or have any other allergies, inform your doctor or pharmacist before using cefotaxime. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Cefotaxime may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefotaxime may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as Coombs' test, urine glucose tests, and serum or urine creatinine tests, potentially causing inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts and kidney function tests, may be conducted while you are using this product. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. It is important to take each dose as scheduled. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Cefotaxime is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It may also be used before and during certain surgeries to prevent infections. This medication belongs to the cephalosporin class of antibiotics. Cefotaxime is administered by injection into a muscle or vein as directed by your doctor. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been properly trained by your healthcare professional. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using this medication for the full prescribed treatment period, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, it may cause loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
